cards.title: Run an agent prompt on a repeating schedule
cards.user_does: Creates an automation with a prompt, an agent and a schedule: hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, or a custom cron or RRULE line, plus a time of day, an optional weekday and a timezone.
cards.user_sees: Kolux starts the agent with that prompt at every due time without being asked, and the automation shows when it will run next.
rules: Hourly fires at the saved minute past every hour; daily at the saved time; weekdays on Monday to Friday only, never on a weekend; weekly on the chosen weekday, where Sunday is day 0.
A custom schedule accepts a standard five-field cron line or an RRULE; malformed, impossible or overlong lines are refused when saving.
Rare but valid dates such as 29 February still produce a next run.
Pasted cron lines with extra spaces or tabs are read as ordinary fields.
A valid cron line that matches no preset is labelled as a custom schedule; presets are stored as their cron equivalent.
Schedule labels are friendly sentences that read the same whatever the computer's locale; a stored schedule that cannot be read shows a safe generic label instead of breaking the page.
The clock checks for due automations about once a minute; paused automations and event-triggered automations are never started by the clock.
Next-run times are computed in the automation's chosen IANA timezone.
In a custom cron line a day field that matches every day (for example */1) counts as unrestricted, so only the other day field narrows the run; weekday 7 is accepted as Sunday.
acceptance: Save a weekdays 09:00 automation on a Friday afternoon → next run reads Monday 09:00.
Type a cron line with minute 61 → save is refused with a validation message.
Save a cron line for 29 February → a next run in the next leap year is shown.
Pause the automation → nothing starts at its next due time; resume → the following due time fires.
cards.compat: CLI trigger values hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, a 5-field cron line or an RRULE (--trigger / --schedule); --time HH:MM; --day 0-6 with Sunday = 0; --timezone takes an IANA zone name.

cards.title: Custom cron editor with a live check and labelled fields
cards.user_does: Switches the schedule picker to Custom and types a cron line, or flips back to a preset.
cards.user_sees: A status line under the field says whether the line is valid and what it means in words; small chips name each of the five fields; weekday and day-of-month pickers use localized names.
rules: Switching to Custom pre-fills the cron line equivalent to the schedule that was selected.
Flipping to a preset and back to Custom keeps what the user had typed.
Field chips and weekday names follow the UI language.
The custom panel shows only the cron field, the five field chips and the status line; it offers no quick-start presets.
acceptance: Pick weekly, Tuesday 10:30, then Custom → the field holds the matching cron line for Tuesday 10:30.
Type nonsense into the field → the status line flags it as invalid and save is blocked.
Switch the UI language → chip labels and weekday names follow it.

cards.title: Time-of-day field with 12-hour entry
cards.user_does: Sets the time an automation runs.
cards.user_sees: Hour and minute boxes with an AM/PM choice; an hourly schedule shows only the minute box.
rules: The time is stored as 24-hour HH:MM; 12:05 AM is 00:05 and 12:00 PM is noon.
New automations start at 09:00.
Typed digits are clamped to a valid value when the box loses focus; an emptied box falls back to its lowest value.
Arrow keys step the value up and down.
acceptance: Enter 1:30 PM → the saved time is 13:30.
Choose hourly → only a minute box is shown.
Type 75 into the minute box and tab away → the box holds 59.

cards.title: Start an automation when something happens in the project
cards.user_does: Sets the trigger to Event and picks one of three events: a pull request opens on a workspace branch, checks fail on a pull request, or an agent finishes in the project.
cards.user_sees: When that event happens in the automation's repo, a run starts with a one-line summary of the event, and a link when one exists, added to the end of the prompt; the run is marked event-triggered and its tooltip names the event.
rules: Only enabled automations whose event kind and repo both match are started.
The first review state Kolux learns for a branch only sets a baseline; nothing fires until it changes, so startup never floods runs.
PR opened fires when a branch goes from no PR to an open one, draft PRs included.
Checks failed fires when checks go from pending to failing; staying failed does not fire again.
Agent finished fires only for a normal finish in a workspace; interrupted finishes, session-boundary finishes and restored-but-unconfirmed rows are ignored.
Each distinct event starts at most one run per automation, and after an event run the automation ignores further events for 5 minutes.
Panes that belong to an automation run never trigger an automation, so an automation cannot set itself off.
Prechecks run before event runs as they do before scheduled runs.

Review events are only noticed while something in Kolux watches that branch (a worktree card or the checks panel): a new PR can take up to about 15 minutes to notice, a check change about a minute; events that happen while Kolux is closed are lost.
The run goes to the automation's own configured workspace, not to the worktree that raised the event.
Switching back to Schedule clears the saved event and recomputes the next run so an old time is not treated as missed.
Hermes jobs never offer the Event option.
Automations saved before event triggers existed load unchanged and keep running on their schedule.
acceptance: Open a draft PR from a workspace branch → within the polling window one run starts and its prompt ends with the event summary.
Raise the same kind of event twice within 5 minutes → only one run.
Let an automation-owned agent finish → no agent-finished automation starts.
Restart Kolux while a PR is already open → nothing fires.
cards.compat: Stored trigger is Schedule or Event; stored event kinds review_opened, review_checks_failed, agent_done (the importer must carry them).

cards.title: Create and edit an automation in one dialog
cards.user_does: Clicks New Automation, or Edit on an existing one, names it, writes the prompt, picks the agent, project and workspace, and saves.
cards.user_sees: A dialog with a large prompt editor and a side column of settings; on save the automation shows in the list at once with its next run, and a footer note says it keeps running until paused.
rules: Workspace choice: run in an existing worktree, or create a fresh worktree for every run branched from a chosen base; the base defaults to the project's default branch and clearing it returns to that default.
The default workspace is the project's main worktree, else its first worktree.
The prompt editor wraps long lines and has a find box; Escape closes the find box first and only then the dialog; undo history survives.
Edit re-reads the saved automation before opening so it never edits a stale copy.
Submitting the same create twice yields one automation, not two.
Save is refused while the project's setup cannot yet be inspected, rather than guessing.
acceptance: Create an automation → it appears in the list immediately, no manual refresh.
Double-click the save button → exactly one automation exists.
Open find in the prompt editor and press Escape → find closes, dialog stays; Escape again → dialog closes.
cards.compat: CLI create/edit flags --name, --prompt, --provider (codex, claude, gemini), --repo (id:, name: or path:), --workspace, --workspace-mode existing|new-per-run, --base-branch, --enabled/--disabled.

cards.title: Start from a template
cards.user_does: Opens Automations with none created yet, or opens the template picker from the editor header.
cards.user_sees: Four starter cards (a weekday repo audit, a weekly release-readiness check, a daily review and an hourly maintenance pass) that pre-fill name, prompt, schedule and grace window, next to a blank option.
rules: Weekday audit runs on weekdays at 09:00 with 12 hours of grace.
Release readiness runs on Thursdays at 14:00 with 24 hours of grace.
Daily review runs at 16:30 with 3 hours of grace.
Hourly maintenance runs at minute 15 with 30 minutes of grace.
Picking a template only fills the form; nothing is saved until the user saves.
acceptance: Empty list → the four template cards and a blank option are shown.
Pick hourly maintenance → schedule is hourly at minute 15 with 30 minutes of grace, nothing saved yet.

cards.title: Missed-run grace window
cards.user_does: Chooses how late a missed run may still start: no grace, 30 minutes, or 1, 3, 12, 24 or 48 hours.
cards.user_sees: If Kolux was closed or asleep at the due time and comes back inside the window, the run starts late; outside it, the history gets one skipped entry saying Kolux was unavailable, and the schedule moves on.
rules: Only the latest overdue occurrence counts; Kolux never replays a backlog of missed runs.
The skipped entry is written even with no grace, so a gap is always visible.
acceptance: Hourly automation with 30 minutes of grace; close Kolux across a due time and reopen 20 minutes later → one late run.
Close Kolux for 3 hours with no grace → one skipped entry, zero runs.

cards.title: Precheck command decides whether a run happens
cards.user_does: Adds a shell command to run before the agent and picks a timeout of 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes.
cards.user_sees: Exit 0 lets the run go ahead; any other exit, or a timeout, records the run as skipped by the precheck with its exit code and captured output.
rules: The command runs in the target repo before scheduled and event runs, never before Run Now.
Default timeout 60 seconds, ceiling 10 minutes; captured output is kept up to 4,000 characters.
A precheck is not run when the project's setup is stale.
Hermes jobs do not offer a precheck.
acceptance: Precheck exits 1 → history shows a precheck skip with exit 1 and the output.
Click Run Now on the same automation → the agent starts, precheck ignored.
Precheck sleeps past its timeout → the run is recorded as timed out.

cards.title: Reuse the same agent session across runs
cards.user_does: For an automation that runs in an existing worktree, turns on session reuse.
cards.user_sees: The next run types its prompt into the agent session left open by the last completed run instead of opening a new tab.
rules: Only available when the workspace mode is an existing worktree; fresh-worktree runs always start a new session.
Reuse needs a session that is still live and idle, from the same automation and worktree, in the exact same pane; otherwise a fresh session starts.
acceptance: Two runs with reuse on and the session left idle → the second run lands in the same tab.
Close that tab before the next due time → the next run opens a fresh one.

cards.title: Choose whether fresh-worktree runs run the project setup
cards.user_does: For a fresh-worktree-per-run automation in a project that has a setup step (kolux.yaml or a project setup hook), decides whether each run's worktree runs it.
cards.user_sees: The setup choice appears only when such a setup exists; each run's new worktree then runs or skips it as chosen.
rules: Hidden for existing-worktree automations and for Hermes or OpenClaw jobs.
Project setup settings take precedence over the repo file.
Older automations with no saved choice open and run as skip.
A failing setup does not stop the agent from starting; an existing worktree never reruns setup.
acceptance: Project with a kolux.yaml setup, fresh worktree per run → setup choice visible.
Project with no setup → no setup choice.

cards.title: Runs start in a background tab without stealing focus
cards.user_does: Keeps working in another worktree while an automation run starts.
cards.user_sees: The run's agent, plus any setup or default tabs, launch in the background in the target worktree; focus stays where the user was; opening that worktree later shows everything printed so far; the run's own tab closes when the agent exits unless the user clicked into it or typed there.
rules: A fresh worktree created for a run is set up and launched without being switched to.
The first time a background tab becomes visible it replays the output it already produced.
The auto-close happens once, only for a tab the run created.
Runs still going when Kolux restarts reattach to their terminal.
acceptance: A scheduled run fires while the user types in another worktree → focus and typing are undisturbed.
Open the run's worktree → the full startup output is visible.
Type in the run's tab, then let the agent exit → the tab stays open.

cards.title: Every run ends with an honest status
cards.user_does: Looks at a run after it was started by the clock, an event or Run Now.
cards.user_sees: The run moves through pending, dispatching and dispatched to completed, or ends as skipped with a reason (precheck, missed, unavailable, needs sign-in) or as failed to dispatch.
rules: A finish signal from a session boundary, a stale idle state or a ready prompt already on screen at dispatch never counts as completion.
If the pane never leaves its pre-dispatch state the run is marked failed, not completed.
When a loss cannot be confirmed the run stays dispatched, and a later real finish still completes it.
After a restart, tracked runs reattach; ones that cannot be found are closed out after a short settle window.
Identical repeated refusals of the same occurrence fold into one entry with a count instead of one entry per check.
acceptance: Kill the agent before it starts working → run shows failed, not completed.
Restart Kolux mid-run → the run keeps tracking and completes when the agent finishes.
A */5 automation whose project is missing for an hour → one folded skipped entry, not twelve.
cards.compat: Stored run statuses pending, dispatching, dispatched, completed, skipped_precheck, skipped_missed, skipped_unavailable, skipped_needs_interactive_auth, dispatch_failed; run trigger scheduled, manual or event (the importer must carry them).

cards.title: Run history for each automation
cards.user_does: Opens an automation's Runs tab and picks a run.
cards.user_sees: A numbered list of runs with trigger, time and status; View run opens the live terminal if it is still there or offers Resume workspace; runs whose worktree was deleted still open from saved output; failed runs offer Rerun; folded rows say how many times they happened and when last.
rules: Run numbers count up per automation starting at 1.
Skipped runs and runs that never got a workspace show their details only.
Worktree names are saved with each run so history still reads correctly after the worktree is deleted.
Rerun appears only on a failed run of an automation that still exists; a fast rerun result stays visible as pending for a moment so it is noticed.
When history cannot be loaded the tab says so with a way to recover, never zero runs.
Up and Down move through runs; Enter opens one.
Pressing Down with no run selected selects the first run; keys pressed with a modifier held or during text composition are ignored.
View run opens a live terminal only while it still belongs to that run; a pane that now shows a different terminal is never opened as the run.
acceptance: Delete a run's worktree → View run shows the saved output with a snapshot notice.
A run fails → Rerun appears; delete the automation → Rerun is gone.
History fails to load → an error with a recovery action, not an empty list.

cards.title: Saved run output and token or cost usage
cards.user_does: Opens a finished run.
cards.user_sees: The latest saved output as plain text, plus tokens and spend for that run; the automation's rows roll usage up across runs.
rules: Saved output drops terminal control sequences and keeps the newest text when it exceeds the size cap.
When the agent's transcript is available it is used instead of raw screen redraws.
Usage is attached only when it can be tied to the run; unknown cost shows as unavailable, never as zero.
Agents with no local usage store are recorded as unsupported without errors.
acceptance: A Codex run with progress bars → saved output has no escape-code noise.
A run with an agent that keeps no usage data → usage reads unavailable, not 0.

cards.title: Runs dashboard across all automations
cards.user_does: Clicks Runs in the Automations toolbar.
cards.user_sees: One table of runs from every automation with automation, trigger, start time and status; a search box; a status filter (in progress, successful, failed, skipped); tiles counting successes and failures over 24 hours and 7 days; Refresh; more rows load 100 at a time; clicking a run opens it full-page with a breadcrumb back to Runs and then Automations.
rules: Runs dated in the future are left out of the 24-hour and 7-day tiles.
A failed load-more keeps the user's place.
A 10,000-run history stays smooth by only drawing visible rows.
Event-triggered runs show a tooltip naming the event.
With no runs at all the table says so plainly.
Leaving the Runs view after loading more rows and coming back reloads from the newest runs.
acceptance: Open the dashboard, open a run, use the breadcrumb → back on the dashboard; again → back on Automations.
Filter to Failed → only failed runs listed.

cards.title: Automations list page with sort, filter and search
cards.user_does: Opens the Automations page.
cards.user_sees: A table of automations with name, schedule or trigger, agent, project, last run (status and how long ago) and next run; the header and first column stay put while scrolling; a toolbar with refresh, Runs and New Automation; each row has a quick-action menu.
rules: Name sorts in natural order; last run sorts newest first with never-run automations last.
Filters: enabled or paused, last-run outcome, and several agents at once.
Search covers name, project, worktree, agent and the first 2,048 characters of the prompt, ignoring case and extra spaces; absurdly long queries are refused.
The search box is focused when the page opens and keeps its text through a refresh.
Opening a row's quick-action menu does not select the row.
Empty states differ for no automations yet, no search match and failed to load; a failed load offers Retry and never claims the list is empty.
Hermes and OpenClaw jobs sort, search and filter in the same table as Kolux automations.
Opening the page selects the first automation and loads its overview and runs; changing the selection loads that automation's runs.
Run status and usage changes appear in the open page as runs progress, without pressing refresh.
acceptance: Search a word that appears only in a prompt → that automation is listed.
Sort by last run → never-run automations sit at the bottom.
Make loading fail → an error with Retry, not a no-automations message.

cards.title: Keyboard control of the list and the detail view
cards.user_does: Uses arrow keys, Enter and Escape on the Automations page.
cards.user_sees: Up and Down move the selection from the list or the search box and Enter opens the automation; Left and Right switch between the Overview and Runs tabs; Escape steps back from detail to list and then closes the page.
rules: Arrow keys and Escape are ignored while typing in a field, inside a dialog, menu or list popup, or with a modifier held.
Escape closes the page only when no dialog or overlay sits above it.
When the selected row disappears, focus moves to a sensible neighbour instead of being lost.
Enter or Space on a focused row opens it; a key pressed on a control inside the row acts on that control only, and clicks inside a row's pop-up menu never count as clicks on the row.
acceptance: Open a dialog over the page and press Escape → only the dialog closes.
Delete the selected automation → focus lands on an adjacent row.

cards.title: Automation overview with an expandable prompt
cards.user_does: Selects an automation and reads its Overview tab.
cards.user_sees: Schedule or trigger, next run, worktree, agent, run count, usage and a plain paused marker when paused; a short prompt is shown in full, a long one is collapsed behind an expand control.
rules: The expand control is reachable by keyboard and keeps focus after use; the prompt text can be selected.
Narrowing the window until the prompt overflows makes the expand control appear.
The run count never reads zero when the history could not be loaded.
Background refreshes keep the prompt's expanded or collapsed state and keep focus on the expand control.
The detail view carries a breadcrumb: Automations, then the automation's name as the current page; clicking Automations returns to the list.
acceptance: A very long prompt at a narrow window → expand control visible; activate it → whole prompt readable.
History fails to load → run count shows unknown, not 0.

cards.title: Run now, pause, edit and delete an automation
cards.user_does: Uses Run Now, the pause/resume switch, Edit or Delete on an automation.
cards.user_sees: Run Now starts a run at once and shows it queued; pause stops future runs until resumed; delete asks for confirmation, then removes the automation and its run history; the list refreshes after each change.
rules: Run Now skips the schedule and the precheck and is recorded as a manual run.
The delete confirmation can be turned off; the preference starts off (always ask).
After a run, the next scheduled time is shown again.
acceptance: Click Run Now on a paused automation → a manual run appears in history.
Delete with confirmation on → a confirm step appears; turn confirmation off → the next delete is immediate.
Pause → no run at the next due time.

cards.title: kolux automations command group
cards.user_does: Runs kolux automations list, show, create, edit, remove, run or runs from a terminal.
cards.user_sees: Readable output, or JSON with --json; create and edit take the same settings as the dialog; remove deletes the automation and its run history; run starts a run now; runs prints history, optionally for one automation.
rules: Without --repo the repo is the Kolux worktree that contains the current folder.
With --workspace the automation runs in that existing worktree; without it, each run gets a new worktree.
edit takes the id as a positional or --id.
Session reuse is accepted only for existing-worktree automations.
Every subcommand answers --help.

create and edit accept --name, --prompt, --provider, --trigger (alias --schedule) taking hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, a five-field cron line or an RRULE, --time HH:MM, --day 0-6 with Sunday 0, --timezone, --enabled or --disabled, --precheck and --precheck-timeout, --repo (id:, name: or path: selector), --workspace, --workspace-mode existing or new-per-run, --base-branch, --missed-run-grace-minutes, and --reuse-session or --fresh-session.
create requires --trigger; no flag sets an event trigger, so event automations are made in the dialog only.
remove deletes at once with no confirmation prompt; show, remove, run and runs take the automation id as a positional or --id.
acceptance: kolux automations create --name Nightly --prompt 'audit' --trigger daily --time 02:00 --json → returns the new id with next run 02:00.
kolux automations remove <id> → the automation and its history are gone from list and runs.
cards.compat: Subcommands list, show <id>, create, edit <id>, remove <id>, run <id>, runs [--id]; flags --json, --help, --name, --prompt, --provider codex|claude|gemini, --precheck, --precheck-timeout, --repo id:|name:|path:, --workspace, --workspace-mode existing|new-per-run, --base-branch, --trigger/--schedule, --time HH:MM, --day 0-6, --timezone, --enabled/--disabled, --missed-run-grace-minutes, --reuse-session/--fresh-session.

cards.title: History keeps the latest 100 runs per automation
cards.user_does: Lets an automation run for a long time.
cards.user_sees: History keeps the newest 100 runs; older finished runs drop off, numbering keeps counting up.
rules: A run still in flight is never dropped, even past the cap.
Run numbers are never reused after old runs are pruned; older runs without numbers get them filled in.
An oversized saved runs file is trimmed when Kolux loads it.
acceptance: Run an automation 105 times → runs 6 to 105 remain and the next is run 106.
A run in progress when the cap is hit still completes and stays listed.

cards.title: Runs refuse cleanly when their target is not ready
cards.user_does: Has an automation whose project or worktree was removed, whose setup is stale, or whose agent account needs a fresh sign-in.
cards.user_sees: The automation shows what is wrong; Run Now is blocked with the reason; scheduled occurrences are recorded as skipped (unavailable or needs sign-in) instead of failing silently.
rules: A refused Run Now never creates a half-started run.
The refusal reason names the missing piece (project, worktree, setup or sign-in).
acceptance: Delete the automation's worktree, click Run Now → a blocked message names the missing worktree; no run appears.
Let a scheduled time pass with the project removed → one skipped entry marked unavailable.

cards.title: Automations entry in the sidebar, off by default
cards.user_does: Turns on the Automations button from View > Appearance in the menu bar or from Appearance settings, or hides it again from the sidebar row's right-click menu.
cards.user_sees: An Automations row in the sidebar that opens the Automations page.
rules: The button is hidden by default on a new install.
The menu checkbox, the settings switch and the right-click hide all change the same setting.
acceptance: Fresh install → no Automations row; tick the menu item → row appears and opens the page.
Right-click the row and hide it → the menu checkbox unticks.

cards.title: Hide or tag worktrees that automations created
cards.user_does: Turns on the sidebar filter that hides automation-created worktrees, or adds the Automation property to worktree cards.
cards.user_sees: Worktrees made by automation runs drop out of the sidebar, or carry an Automation tag on their card.
rules: Jumping to an automation-created worktree (for example from View run) clears the hiding filter so the worktree is visible.
acceptance: Filter on, then View run on a fresh-worktree run → the filter turns off and the worktree is shown.

cards.title: Hermes and OpenClaw cron jobs beside Kolux automations
cards.user_does: Has the Hermes or OpenClaw agent installed on this computer and opens Automations, or picks Hermes in the create dialog's Kolux / Hermes switch.
cards.user_sees: That tool's cron jobs appear in the list, labelled as running on this computer, each with a pause/resume switch; Hermes jobs can be run, edited, deleted and created from Kolux; OpenClaw jobs can be run and deleted but not edited; Hermes run history is read from its cron output into titled sections.
rules: Hermes jobs need a cron schedule and offer no agent, session reuse, event trigger or precheck options.
A warning appears when the tool's command is not on the PATH.
External jobs are left out of the agent filter.
Only log files inside the tool's own home folder are read.

Hermes and OpenClaw job lists are cached and reload on Refresh; the Kolux list finishes loading even when one of their checks hangs; their checks run a few at a time and wait while Kolux's own automation work is running.
acceptance: With Hermes installed, create a Hermes automation → a Hermes cron job exists and shows in the list.
Pause an OpenClaw job from Kolux → OpenClaw reports it paused; no Edit action is offered.

cards.title: Automations on SSH hosts and paired Kolux servers
cards.user_does: Picks a remote host for an automation, filters the list by host, or moves an automation between hosts.
cards.user_sees: Automations from many hosts in one list with host badges, health and recovery actions, orphan handling, and runs dispatched by a headless remote Kolux.
rules: Covers the host picker and filter, host catalog and diagnostics, owner fencing, orphaned automations, SSH re-adoption, cross-host moves, headless serve dispatch, and the CLI flags --pairing-code, --environment and --project --host.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: area 18 (SSH hosts, paired runtime servers, headless serve) is dropped, so automations run on this computer only. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Hermes and OpenClaw jobs on remote hosts
cards.user_does: Views or manages Hermes or OpenClaw cron jobs that live on an SSH host or paired server.
cards.user_sees: Remote jobs listed per host with their run history fetched through the relay.
rules: Remote probing, scoping and paged remote run history go with area 18.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: remote hosts and relay are area 18, dropped; only local Hermes and OpenClaw stay. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Linear, Jira and GitLab as automation sources
cards.user_does: Attaches a Linear issue as source context to an automation, or relies on GitLab pipelines to fire the checks-failed event.
cards.user_sees: The automation shows the linked issue as its source; GitLab merge requests and pipelines count as review events.
rules: Includes the --source-context CLI flag and Linear source display.
Linear and Jira event triggers were never built (they needed a poller).
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: Linear, Jira and GitLab integrations are cut by table 1b, so review events and source context are GitHub-only. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Automations section in Settings
cards.user_does: Opens Settings > Automations.
cards.user_sees: The sidebar-button switch, a three-step explanation of how automations work, and a button that opens the Automations page.
rules: The Automations page itself stays; the sidebar-button switch already also lives in Appearance and the menu bar.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: table 1b removes the automations settings section; the feature keeps its own page and the switch stays under Appearance. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

notes: Entry point UNKNOWN in the redesign: the sidebar Automations button defaults to off and no top-bar entry was found; today the page is reached via the sidebar row, the View menu toggle or the cut settings section.
Mis-mapped tests: browser-client-automation-protocol and browser-automation-bootstrap-lease belong to area 13, not 09.
About half of area 09's test titles are area-18 host machinery (host catalog, owner fencing, orphans, SSH re-adoption, runtime servers, scale gates); carded as two D items, not per behaviour.
Hermes and OpenClaw integrations are third-party tool integrations not named in the owner cuts; tiered P1, owner should confirm keep or cut.

Event automations v1 gaps: runs land in the configured workspace rather than the triggering worktree, and review events depend on something polling the branch; GitLab pipeline events go with the GitLab cut.
Unshipped ideas AGENT-14 (error-feed and ticket triggers) and PROD-8 (GitHub issue triage automation) are in improvement-cards only; not carded.
